venues.name: McDowell Grove Forest Preserve

venues.age: All ages — flat trail, paved/stroller-friendly sections

venues.name: Danada Forest Preserve

venues.name: Springbrook Prairie

venues.name: Riverview Farmstead Preserve

venues.name: The Fun Playce

venues.name: Playroom Cafe Naperville

venues.note: Montessori-inspired indoor playground for the 0–6 set, with a real cafe (coffee, smoothies, kid meals) for parents.

venues.age: 1–12 (admits up to 17, but play structures suit younger kids best)

venues.name: Kids Empire Bolingbrook

venues.age: 1–12 (admits up to 17, but play structures suit younger kids best)

venues.note: Sister location to Hyper Kidz Wheaton — same unlimited-time play model, socks required.

venues.note: Forest Preserve District of Will County nature center with prairie/forest/savanna trails and fishing access.

venues.age: All ages (Children's Garden best for young kids)

venues.name: Wil-O-Way Commons Park
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily

venues.name: Frontier Sports Complex

venues.note: Large sports complex behind Neuqua Valley HS with a renovated central playground, skate park, and pond, alongside ball fields, courts, and picnic shelters.

venues.name: Wil-O-Way Park
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Small neighborhood park next to Wil-O-Way Commons with a playground, baseball backstop, and basketball courts.
venues.age: All ages

venues.age: All ages — slides and swings for younger and older kids, sandbox for toddlers

venues.name: Country Lakes Park
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Inclusive playground (renovated 2017) designed for kids of all abilities, plus a sled hill and multi-use trails.
venues.age: All ages

venues.name: Burlington Park
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily

venues.age: All ages — quiet nature walk, no playground equipment

venues.name: St. James Farm Forest Preserve
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Historic McCormick horse farm with scenic trails, sculpture-dotted grounds, and a public indoor riding arena.

venues.age: All ages for trails; arena riding is age 12+ (under 18 must ride with an adult)

venues.name: Greene Valley Forest Preserve
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: 13.8 miles of trails and a 190-ft scenic overlook with Chicago skyline views, open weekends May–October.
venues.age: All ages — best for older kids/bikers on the longer trails

venues.name: Waterfall Glen Forest Preserve
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily

venues.age: All ages — best for older kids/cyclists on the long perimeter loop

venues.name: Warrenville Grove
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily
venues.note: Riverside woodland preserve along the West Branch DuPage River with picnic areas and a trail past a small dam.
venues.age: All ages — flat, short trail good for young kids

venues.name: Goodrich Woods
venues.hours: Dawn–dusk daily

venues.age: All ages — short (0.5 mi) easy loop, good for young kids

venues.name: Centennial Beach

venues.cost: $8–17/person, age & residency-based (youth 3–17: $8 resident/$15 nonresident; adult: $10/$17; discounted $5/$9 after 5 PM)

venues.name: Naper Settlement

venues.age: 4–12, though younger kids can tag along

venues.cost: Museum & garden admission free; parking $5/car ($10 weekends & holidays May–Sep), free the first Wednesday of each month
venues.age: All ages

venues.name: Fermilab's Lederman Science Center

venues.age: 5–14 (many exhibits geared toward 10+)

venues.name: Phillips Park Zoo

venues.note: Small, free municipal zoo of mostly North American animals inside Phillips Park — an easy 30–60 minute visit.
venues.age: All ages

venues.name: Shedd Aquarium

venues.cost: Chicago residents $19.95 adult general admission; non-residents from $38.95 adult / $28.95 child (under 3 free); total-experience passes cost more
venues.age: All ages

venues.note: Massive natural-history museum — SUE the T. rex, Egyptian mummies, and a real gem hall. Free for Illinois residents on select Wednesdays (reservation required).
venues.cost: ~$30 adult / ~$21 Chicago resident general admission, discounted child pricing; free for IL residents select Wednesdays
venues.age: All ages

venues.hours: 9:30 AM–4 PM daily; closed Thanksgiving & Christmas
venues.note: Huge hands-on science museum — real U-505 submarine, coal mine, and dome theater. Formerly "Museum of Science and Industry"; still commonly called MSI.
venues.cost: $25.95 adult / $14.95 child (3–11); Chicago residents get $9/$5 off; free for Illinois residents select days
venues.age: All ages

venues.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
venues.hours: 10 AM–5 PM daily (grounds open earlier/later seasonally)
venues.note: One of the last free zoos in the country — no ticket needed, 200-plus species on 49 acres in the heart of the city.
venues.age: All ages

venues.name: Chicago Children's Museum
venues.hours: Mon, Wed, Thu 10 AM–2 PM; Fri–Sun 10 AM–5 PM; closed Tue
venues.note: Hands-on museum at Navy Pier built for young kids; same admission price for adults and children.
venues.cost: $25/person (ages 1+); $21/person with IL residency ID; $5/person for up to 6 with EBT/WIC; free under 1

venues.name: Chicago Botanic Garden

venues.cost: Garden admission free; parking $10/car (free for members)
venues.age: All ages

venues.note: Lakefront planetarium and astronomy museum with sky shows and skyline views; free for Illinois residents on select days.
venues.cost: Museum Entry (no sky show) $25 adult / $13 child; sky-show bundles cost more
venues.age: 5–12 (sky shows recommended 5+)

venues.note: Indoor LEGO playground in a Schaumburg mall — rides, a 4D theater, and build zones; skews toward younger kids per reviews.

venues.age: 3–10 (older kids/teens may find it babyish per reviews)
